evidence.quote: We control for additional firm-level characteristics in the regression, such as size, defined as the log of market value of equity (SIZE), the most recent year's annual capex (LAG_CAPX), the earnings surprise for the most recent quarter (SURP) defined as the quarter's earnings-per-share minus that of the same quarter of the previous year, and an indicator variable to denote capex announcements that are accompanied by earnings announcements (EA_DUM).

MKTRET denotes market returns measured using the S&P 500 index on the capex forecast date. CAR_PRE denotes pseudo-market reactions defined as the 5-day market reaction around a nonforecast date, defined as 2 weeks prior to the capex forecast date.

evidence.quote: Columns 1 and 3 present results for sample of capex forecasts with lower bid-ask spreads in the event-window (i.e., days [-2, 2]) as compared to the pre-event window (i.e., days [-10, -3]), and Columns 2 and 4 present results for forecasts with higher bid-ask spreads.

Models 3 and 4 present results based on splitting CAR into two variables: CAR_POS denoting positive market reactions, and zero otherwise; and CAR_NEG denoting negative market reactions, and zero otherwise.
